title: Active-arrow lifting fibers detect weak approximation
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the ordinary and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $f:M\to O$ be an inert-preserving map of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads with $O$ ordinary. For $C\in M$ and an active edge $\alpha:X\to f(C)$, let
$$\mathcal L_f(C,\alpha)=M_{/C}\times_{O_{/f(C)}}\{\alpha\}$$
be the homotopy-pullback lifting infinity category, retaining the comparison equivalence and all its coherences. In the ordered-join model, this is represented by the full subcomplex of the coherent factorization model on vertices whose first edge is an equivalence in $O$. Then $f$ is a weak approximation in the sense of [def-coef-operadic-weak-approximation] if and only if this equivalence-edge lifting model is weakly contractible for every $C\in M$ and every active $\alpha:X\to f(C)$. No space assumption on positive-arity fibers and no categorical-fibration assumption on $f$ is imposed; the zero-fiber convention of the cited generalized-operad definition remains in force.

source.place: Erratum Proposition E.0.2 (the corrected active-slice criterion, not the uncorrected Corollary A.6.9) Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic result.

proof.text: First let $g:M'\to O$ be an inert-preserving categorical fibration and use the specified join-slice model of [def-coef-operadic-weak-approximation]: with $B=O_{/g(C)}$, it is the full subcategory $\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)\subseteq M'_{/C}\times_B B_{\alpha/}$ on inert first edges $\gamma$. Its simplices retain the entire coherent triangle. In particular, the comparison edges $h$ are unrestricted; we do not replace this full subcategory by one retaining only inert comparison edges. If $\alpha$ is active over $[n]\to[k]$, write its opposite order map as $\phi:[k]\to[n]$, with $\phi(0)=0$ and $\phi(k)=n$. For a factorization $\alpha\simeq g(\beta)\gamma$ with $\gamma$ inert, the base of $\gamma$ is opposite to an interval inclusion $j:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ and $\phi=j\psi$ for the opposite base map $\psi$ of $\beta$. The image of $j$ contains $0$ and $n$, so $j$ is the identity and $\gamma$ is cocartesian over an identity, hence an equivalence. The latter follows also from the cocartesian mapping-square criterion: precomposition with $\gamma$ is an equivalence on every mapping space, so it has an inverse with the two inverse triangles. Thus the objects of $\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)$ are exactly $(\beta,\gamma)$ with $\gamma:X\simeq g(D)$ and $g(\beta)\gamma\simeq\alpha$. Inverting $\gamma$ gives an equivalence $g(\beta)\simeq\alpha$ in $O_{/g(C)}$, and inverting again is the inverse construction. On the join-slice model, a simplex consists of an entire family of these triangles, and inversion of an equivalence in the slice acts on the family and commutes coherently with its face and degeneracy restrictions. The equivalence-edge coslice based at $\alpha$ models the homotopy fiber over $\alpha$: it retains a comparison equivalence and all its coherent simplices. Thus these inverse operations identify $\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)\simeq\mathcal L_g(C,\alpha)$. No assertion that $\beta$ was active was used in deriving $j=1$.

source.place: Definition A.6.1 and the active-arrow case in Proposition A.6.3 / Erratum Proposition E.0.2

proof.text: For an arbitrary $\alpha:X\to g(C)$ over $[n]\to[k]$, let $\phi:[k]\to[n]$ be its opposite base map. Set $a=\phi(0)$, $b=\phi(k)$ and $r=b-a$. The map $\phi$ factors as $[k]\xrightarrow{\phi-a}[r]\xrightarrow{i\mapsto a+i}[n]$, with the first map preserving endpoints and the second an interval inclusion. Choose the inert cocartesian lift $\delta:X\to X_0$ in $O$ over that inclusion, as provided by the operad axioms. By the cocartesian mapping-square criterion, the space of factorizations $\alpha\simeq\alpha_0\delta$ with $\alpha_0:X_0\to g(C)$ over the specified active base map is contractible. Fix such data. Inside $\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)$ let $\mathcal A_0$ be the full subcategory of objects for which the base interval of $\gamma$ is precisely $[a,b]$. The same criterion in $O$ identifies each such $\gamma$ with $u\delta$ for a uniquely specified equivalence $u:X_0\simeq g(D)$, up to a contractible space of coherent choices. The equivalence is forced because both $\gamma$ and $\delta$ are cocartesian over the same base arrow: precomposition by each identifies the same mapping-space fibers. Removing $\delta$ therefore identifies $\mathcal A_0$ with $\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha_0)$, and Step 1 identifies this with $\mathcal L_g(C,\alpha_0)$. These comparisons are on the coherent factorization data, including their mapping spaces, not on their isomorphism classes.

source.place: Proposition A.6.3 / Erratum Proposition E.0.2: explicit minimal-interval factorization for an arbitrary arrow

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-operadic-minimal-interval-reflection] to the same $g,C,\alpha$ and its interval $[a,b]$ from Step 2. It supplies the coherent adjunction $R\dashv i$ for the full inclusion $i:\mathcal A_0\to\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)$, its unit $1\to iR$ and equivalence counit $Ri\simeq1$. Its hypotheses hold: $g$ is the inert-preserving categorical fibration fixed in Step 1, $M'$ is generalized, $O$ is ordinary, and $\alpha$ is arbitrary. Its factorization category is exactly the full join-slice category used here, with unrestricted comparison edges. In the explicit description of its unit, an object whose inert interval is $[t,t+m]$ is restricted along $[a-t,b-t]\subseteq[m]$. Thus its image lies in precisely the subcategory $\mathcal A_0$ identified in Step 2.

source.place: Proposition A.6.3 / Erratum Proposition E.0.2: write out the inert-restriction reflection behind the all-arrows criterion

proof.text: The unit $1\to iR$ is a simplicial map $\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)$. On realization its prism gives a homotopy between $1$ and $|i||R|$; the counit $Ri\simeq1$ gives the other homotopy. This prism is obtained by triangulating each $|\Delta^s|\times[0,1]$ into its $s+1$ standard simplices and applying the displayed simplicial map; the restrictions agree on common faces. Hence $|i|$ and $|R|$ are homotopy inverses. Step 2 now shows that $\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)$ is weakly contractible if $\mathcal L_g(C,\alpha_0)$ is. Consequently, if all active lifting categories are weakly contractible, all factorization categories for arbitrary arrows are weakly contractible, and the categorical-fibration clause of [def-coef-operadic-weak-approximation] makes $g$ a weak approximation. Conversely that clause applied to active arrows and Step 1 gives weak contractibility of all active lifting categories. This proves both directions for categorical fibrations. When $k=0$ one has $a=b$ and $r=0$; when $n=0$ every interval here is $[0,0]$, so both cases are included.

source.place: Proposition A.6.3 / Erratum Proposition E.0.2: weak contractibility via the explicit reflection

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-generalized-operadic-fibration-replacement] to the original inert-preserving map $f:M\to O$. Its hypotheses are the small generalized-operad hypotheses of the item (an ordinary $O$ is also generalized). It gives a small generalized operad $M'$, an operadic equivalence $e:M\to M'$ and an inert-preserving categorical fibration $g:M'\to O$ with the strict equality $f=g\circ e$ of simplicial maps, all over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and in the original universe. Its conclusion includes the Kan zero fiber, Segal and incidence axioms and an inert-preserving quasi-inverse for $e$. Hence this is a representative to which the categorical-fibration argument of Steps 1--4 applies. The active lifting condition is transferred in Steps 6--7.

source.place: Definition A.6.1, existence of the equivalence--categorical-fibration replacement used in Proposition E.0.2; explicit Joyal replacement and transfer of operadic axioms

proof.text: For any operadic equivalence $e:M\to M'$ with the strict equality $f=g\circ e$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, choose a quasi-inverse $r$ and coherent inverse transformations. On slices, $e$ sends $a:D\to C$ to $e(a):e(D)\to e(C)$. An inverse sends $b:D'\to e(C)$ to the composite $r(D')\xrightarrow{r(b)}re(C)\simeq C$. The inverse transformations give the two inverse comparisons on these slices, including their coherent triangles. Apply the same operations to the equivalence from the image arrow to the chosen target edge $\alpha$: its image under $e$ has the same image under $g$ because $f=ge$; in the inverse construction use $f r=g e r\simeq g$ from the counit of $e,r$. This gives inverse functors on the homotopy-pullback lifting categories. Thus $\mathcal L_f(C,\alpha)\simeq\mathcal L_g(e(C),\alpha')$, where $\alpha'=\alpha$ since $f(C)=g(e(C))$. To cover objects outside the chosen image, choose $t:e(C)\simeq C'$ for each $C'\in M'$ and send an active $\alpha':X\to g(C')$ to $g(t)^{-1}\alpha'$. Postcomposition with $t,t^{-1}$ gives the corresponding inverse slice functors. Equivalences lie over identity base arrows, so this operation preserves activeness. Hence all active lifting categories for $f$ are weakly contractible if and only if all those for $g$ are. Each functor equivalence used here preserves weak contractibility: its coherent inverse transformations yield homotopies on geometric realizations by the prism construction of Step 4.

source.place: Definition A.6.1 / Proposition E.0.2: explicit inverse functors for equivalence transport and essential-surjectivity of the targets

proof.text: If $f$ is a weak approximation, its defining clause supplies an exact factorization $f=g\circ e$ through an operadic equivalence and a categorical-fibration weak approximation $g$, all over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Step 4 gives the active lifting condition for $g$, and Step 6 gives it for $f$. Conversely, if $f$ satisfies the active lifting condition, use the representative constructed in Step 5. Step 6 gives the condition for its categorical fibration $g$, and Step 4 makes $g$ a weak approximation. The strict equality $f=g\circ e$ supplied by Step 5 is exactly the equality required by the current definition, so this representative is a witness for the general clause of [def-coef-operadic-weak-approximation]. Therefore $f$ is a weak approximation. This proves the asserted equivalence with no categorical-fibration hypothesis on $f$ and no positive-arity space hypothesis.

statement_change.what: The recorded conclusion used the unrestricted coherent factorization model. It always contains the identity first edge at the terminal vertex, so it is contractible independently of f and cannot represent the homotopy pullback over an active arrow. The source lifting category retains an equivalence in the slice; the corrected statement uses the full subcomplex whose first edge is an equivalence, which is the ordered-join model of that homotopy pullback.
